newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU BSE inquiry meets to vote on Commission censure.
newsitem.headline: EU BSE inquiry meets to vote on Commission censure.

text.p: A European Parliament committee of inquiry met on Wednesday to consider a threat to censure the European Commission for mishandling the mad cow crisis.

The 19-member cross-party committee was also due to vote at a two-day meeting on 253 other amendments to a report by Spanish Socialist Manuel Medina Ortega criticising the EU executive and Britain, where mad cow disease originated.
If agreed by the committee, the threat of censure action and the report as a whole will be put to the vote in the full parliament on February 19.

The proposal for a censure motion, which will be examined on Thursday, gives the Commission until December to apply the corrective measures, including a reorganisation of EU veterinary services and a shake-up of scientific advisory committees, demanded by the parliament.

If not, the parliament would immediately call a vote on a censure motion which would force Commission President Jacques Santer and his 19 colleagues to resign if it gets the required two-thirds majority.
Santer told the inquiry in mid-January the Commission planned similar changes which are expected to be announced later this month.
Parliamentary sources said it was still unclear what sanctions would be sought against Britain. Any legal action against Britain would have to be taken through the Commission.

The draft report identified 13 points of alleged negligence, including failure to enforce properly a ban on exports of animal feed containing infected meat and bone meal, pressing Brussels to avoid inspecting British slaughterhouses between 1990-94 and ignoring scientific warnings.

The mad cow crisis hit the headlines in March 1996 when London admitted that the fatal cattle brain disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) could spread to humans who ate infected beef. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
